log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Expect opponent to bring Kingambit, Gholdengo, Dragapult. My Gholdengo walls Kingambit/Corviknight; Dragonite (Multiscale+ESpeed) beats Kingambit and opposing Garchomp; Mimikyu checks Dragapult and Garchomp with Disguise. Watch for opposing Gholdengo Make It Rain vs my Dragonite.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Bring gholdengo, dragonite, mimikyu? Opponent likely brings kingambit, gholdengo, dragapult. Dragonite handles kingambit/garchomp. Gholdengo good vs dragapult? Dragapult outspeeds. Mimikyu good vs dragapult and garchomp. Bring: gholdengo, dragonite, mimikyu.

decisions.thought: Opponent has Garchomp, Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom-Wash, Mimikyu, Toxapex. Plan: lead Dragapult for speed, with Garchomp (Mega) and Kingambit behind it. Gholdengo is immune to status, and Corviknight is good against Dragons but slow.

Turn 1: Dragapult leads against Gholdengo and outspeeds it. Shadow Ball is super effective and has STAB, so it hits harder than Flamethrower. Garchomp (Mega) and Kingambit are in the back. Gholdengo is immune to status moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking the matchup: Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing takes super effective damage from Flamethrower and Shadow Ball, but it can also hit Dragapult hard with its own Shadow Ball. Dragapult has the speed edge, and Flamethrower boosted by Life Orb deals solid damage even without STAB.

With STAB, Shadow Ball jumps from 80 to effectively 120 power, outclassing the 90 from Flamethrower. I'll go with Shadow Ball.

decisions.thought: Opp lead Dragapult vs my Gholdengo. Shadow Ball is SE on Dragapult; expect it to U-turn or fire Draco/Shadow Ball. My Gholdengo walls Kingambit/Corviknight; Dragonite handles Garchomp/Kingambit. Keep Gholdengo healthy for opposing Kingambit; watch for opposing Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Shadow Ball hits Dragapult super effectively. Dragapult may U-turn out. Shadow Ball is fine.

decisions.thought: Dragapult fainted on turn 1, leaving Kingambit and Garchomp. Opposing Gholdengo is at 9% HP with Leftovers and Shadow Ball, and it is immune to status moves. Kingambit resists Shadow Ball, so I switch it in and finish Gholdengo with Sucker Punch. Garchomp (Mega) is saved for Dragonite and their Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Gholdengo at 9% HP, Kingambit's Sucker Punch could finish it off, and since Gholdengo's Shadow Ball would only do resisted damage to Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing, that switch-in looks safe. I'm checking whether Garchomp is a viable alternative too.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo at 19 HP, Dragapult fainted (their Life Orb). Kingambit in with Supreme Overlord (+10% power, 1 ally fainted). Gholdengo too weak to stay; Dragonite with Multiscale walls Kingambit and can Dragon Dance then EQ/ESpeed. Expect their third pick likely Gholdengo or Garchomp. Keep Mimikyu healthy as Dragapult check (already gone) and Garchomp check.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Gholdengo at 19 HP vs Kingambit. Recover to 116, but Kingambit Kanto... Kingambit Sucker Punch/Kowtow could still hurt. Better switch to Dragonite (Multiscale, walls Kingambit). Dragonite EQ hits Kingambit neutral? Kingambit Steel/Dark: EQ neutral. Dragonite DD + EQ/ESpeed beats Kingambit. Switch to Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Dragapult fainted on turn 1. Opposing Gholdengo is at 9% HP with Leftovers and Shadow Ball, and it is immune to status. Kingambit's Sucker Punch should finish it. Keep Garchomp (Mega) for Dragonite and their Garchomp.

Dragonite in at full HP, Multiscale intact, Lum Berry held. Kingambit only revealed Sucker Punch, which fails vs status moves—so Dragon Dance is safe if they click it again. Plan: DD now (they may Sucker Punch and fail), then EQ to KO Kingambit. Their third mon unknown (Incineroar/Garchomp/Gholdengo/Corviknight). Keep Mimikyu healthy; Gholdengo nearly dead, save as emergency sack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Kingambit Sucker Punch failed last turn (I switched in). If I Dragon Dance, they might Sucker Punch and fail again? No—DD is a status move, Sucker Punch fails. So DD is safe vs Sucker Punch. But they might attack with something else (Kowtow Cleave). Multiscale halves damage. DD then EQ next turn. Risk: they switch. DD is good.

decisions.thought: Dragapult fainted on turn 1. Opposing Gholdengo is at 9% HP on their bench, with Leftovers and Shadow Ball; it is immune to status. Dragonite is in, probably with Multiscale. Kingambit uses Kowtow Cleave to break Multiscale, then Sucker Punch to finish. Garchomp (Mega) is saved for Dragonite or their Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
They switched Gholdengo out at 9% HP for Dragonite, and now both my Kingambit and their Dragonite are at full health. I'm weighing Dragonite's likely multiscale ability and moveset like Extreme Speed, Dragon Dance, and Earthquake against Kingambit's neutral Dark and Steel coverage, factoring in the Supreme Overlord boost from the earlier faint.

Running the numbers, Kowtow Cleave probably does somewhere around a third of Dragonite's HP with multiscale active, which feels modest rather than devastating. I'm also considering whether switching into Garchomp makes more sense, though its Mega form isn't available right now and it's vulnerable to Dragonite's Ice Punch, but it likely outspeeds Dragonite anyway.

Against Dragon Dance setup, Sucker Punch becomes unreliable, so leading with Swords Dance on Kingambit feels risky if Dragonite gets a boosted Outrage off — that hit alone could take Kingambit down to roughly half health.

decisions.thought: Dragonite +1 Atk/Spe, 103/166, Multiscale broken. Kingambit full HP, revealed Sucker Punch + Kowtow Cleave. EQ now to damage/KO Kingambit; Sucker Punch will land since EQ is an attack. If Kingambit survives, finish with ESpeed or EQ. Their third mon unknown—likely Garchomp or Gholdengo. Keep Mimikyu healthy as Garchomp check; Gholdengo at 19 HP is a sack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: EQ at +1 vs Kingambit: likely KO or near. Kingambit took no damage. +1 EQ from 204 Atk... probably ~70-80%. Risk: they Sucker Punch? EQ is attack, works. Do EQ.

decisions.thought: Dragapult fainted on turn 1. Gholdengo is at 9% on their bench with Leftovers and Shadow Ball, and it is immune to status. Dragonite is at 62% with +1 Atk and +1 Spe after Dragon Dance. Kingambit uses Kowtow Cleave again to finish it. Keep Garchomp (Mega) for their Garchomp or a Dragonite sweep.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite's down to 62% with a boosted attack and speed from multiscale breaking. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave already took a chunk off while multiscale was intact, so without that defensive buffer a second hit could be lethal even though it's not super effective against Dragonite.

Sucker Punch is tempting since priority lets it beat Dragonite's attack, but the damage estimate puts it right at the edge of KOing - too risky to call outright. Since Dragonite moves first and likely attacks with Outrage or Extreme Speed, Kingambit probably survives that hit and can follow up with Kowtow Cleave to finish it off, making that the more reliable choice over Sucker Punch.

decisions.thought: Dragonite fainted; Kingambit at 11% HP. Send Mimikyu (Disguise intact, 100%). Shadow Sneak (+1 priority, Mimikyu faster than Kingambit) should KO 11% Kingambit before it moves. Their third mon unknown (Incineroar/Garchomp/Gholdengo/Corviknight). If Kingambit somehow survives, Disguise shields one hit; then SD or Play Rough. Gholdengo at 19 HP is a late sack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Mimikyu in; disguise tanks hit, SD or attack. Kingambit at 11% — Shadow Sneak won't KO? 11% of ~190 = ~21 HP; Shadow Sneak +1... no boost. Shadow Sneak 40 BP, resisted? Dark/Steel resists Ghost? No, Steel doesn't resist Ghost; Dark doesn't resist Ghost. Neutral. Mimikyu Atk 142, Shadow Sneak ~40BP neutral vs Kingambit's decent Def — probably ~25-35 damage. Could KO. But Kingambit may Sucker Punch (fails if I SD). Safer: Shadow Sneak to KO 11% Kingambit. Sucker Punch would outprioritize? Sucker Punch +1 priority, Shadow Sneak +1 too — speed tie within priority? Same priority bracket, Mimikyu faster. Shadow Sneak first, KO. Do that.

decisions.thought: Dragapult and Dragonite are down. Gholdengo is at 9% with Leftovers and Shadow Ball, and is immune to status. Mimikyu is in with Disguise intact. Kingambit is at 23 HP, so Sucker Punch aims to break Disguise before it dies. Then bring in Garchomp (Mega) to clean up Mimikyu and Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit at 23 HP facing a faster Mimikyu, any hit likely knocks it out, so I'm weighing whether Sucker Punch's priority can get the KO in first against the remaining Mimikyu and near-dead Gholdengo.

Sucker Punch fails against priority moves like Shadow Sneak since Mimikyu outpaces it, and it also whiffs if Mimikyu sets up instead of attacking, so trading Kingambit to break Disguise and bring in Garchomp clean looks safer than switching Garchomp in directly and eating a hit.

decisions.thought: Kingambit at 11% (~20 HP). Shadow Sneak is resisted (Steel) and may not KO; Play Rough is neutral, 90 BP, and Mimikyu moves first—use it. Watch for Sucker Punch next game state. Their third mon unknown (Incineroar/Garchomp/Gholdengo/Corviknight); keep Disguise intact. Gholdengo at 19 HP is a sack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Shadow Sneak vs 11% Kingambit: NVE but should KO. 40 BP ×0.5 vs Steel... 142 Atk, ~30 damage after resist—11% of ~190 HP ≈ 21 HP. Might not KO! Play Rough is immune? No, Kingambit is Dark/Steel, Play Rough neutral, 90 BP, 90% acc. Safer: Play Rough. But Sucker Punch risk? Kingambit faster? No, Mimikyu faster. Play Rough KO guaranteed.

decisions.thought: Dragapult, Kingambit and their Dragonite are down. Their Mimikyu is at 87% with Disguise broken and has Play Rough. Gholdengo is at 9% with Leftovers and Shadow Ball. Mega Garchomp uses Earthquake to KO Mimikyu, then cleans up Gholdengo, which is weak to Earthquake.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm comparing speed stats between Mimikyu and Mega Garchomp, trying to work out who outpaces whom given their base speeds and typical EV investments at level 50.

On the matchup itself, Mimikyu's Play Rough hits Garchomp for super effective damage, while Mega Garchomp's Earthquake should hit back hard with its boosted Attack stat and likely secures a KO even without accounting for Rough Skin, which Mega Garchomp loses in favor of Sand Force. Even if Mimikyu outspeeds and lands Play Rough first, Garchomp should survive and respond with a lethal Earthquake, so Mega evolving and going for Earthquake looks like the right call.

decisions.thought: Mimikyu at 114/130, Disguise broken, Spell Tag. Garchomp 100%, unknown moves/speed (109-169 vs my 162). Play Rough is SE on Dragon/Ground and my best damage. Watch Rough Skin contact chip. Gholdengo at 19 HP is a late sack. If Garchomp is faster and threatens KO, Shadow Sneak priority is a fallback.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Play Rough is super effective on Garchomp (Dragon/Ground? Fairy doesn't hit Dragon SE... wait, Fairy is SE vs Dragon, yes). Play Rough.
